title: Invariant affine charts of an admissible finite-group scheme quotient
statement: Let $M$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let a finite group $H$ act on $M$ by scheme automorphisms. Assume the action is admissible, meaning that every orbit of underlying points is contained in an affine open subscheme. Then there is a categorical quotient $q:M\to Q$ in schemes. Categorical means that every $H$-invariant scheme morphism $M\to Z$ factors uniquely through $q$. The map $q$ is affine, integral and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], its topology is the orbit-space topology, and its geometric fibres are $H$-orbits. There is a covering of $M$ by $H$-stable affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ such that $q(W)$ is open affine, $q^{-1}q(W)=W$, and the restriction $W\to q(W)$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}(B^H)$, where $B^H=\{b\in B:h(b)=b\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. For every affine open $V\subseteq Q$, its inverse image is affine and $\mathcal O_Q(V)$ is the invariant subring of $\mathcal O_M(q^{-1}V)$ under the canonical map. Restriction to an invariant open of $M$ is its categorical quotient onto the corresponding open of $Q$. No finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis and no module-finiteness conclusion for $q$ are imposed.
